uncited: This method identifies the outer boundary of a Minkowski sum by propagating a "filled" state from the exterior into the interior volume, stopping when blocked by the object's boundary.

It builds on [Slice Filling with BFS Propagation](1909-slice-filling-with-bfs-propagation.md) by using a global iterative flood fill rather than slice-local propagation to determine which voxels are outside the Minkowski sum.
Represents the current state of the flood fill.
Value 1 indicates a voxel is filled (exterior), 0 indicates empty (interior).
Represents the boundary of the Minkowski sum object.
Value 1 indicates a boundary voxel, 0 otherwise.
Initialize $T_o$ by subtracting the intersection with the target boundary: $T_o \leftarrow T_o - (T_o \cap T_b)$.
This ensures boundary voxels are not marked as filled exterior.
Identify initial candidates: For all voxels $(i, j, k)$, if at least one neighbor has value 1 in $T_o$, set $T_{mask}(i, j, k) = 1$.
If $T_o(i, j, k) = 0$ and $T_b(i, j, k) = 0$, then set $T_o(i, j, k) = 1$ and $T_{new}(i, j, k) = 1$.
Identify next candidates: For all voxels $(i, j, k)$, if at least one neighbor has value 1 in $T_{new}$, set $T_{mask}(i, j, k) = 1$.
Check termination: If $\forall (i, j, k), T_{new}(i, j, k) = 0$, exit loop.
- Performance is determined by shape complexity.
A post-processing step to compute the correct surface voxelization by identifying primitive voxels adjacent to the identified outer voxels.
- **Time Complexity:** Determined by shape complexity and volumetric resolution.
- **Memory Complexity:** Requires storage for $T_o$, $T_b$, $T_{new}$, and $T_{mask}$, all of size $N_x \times N_y \times N_z$.
